_note: Hand review of every mapping the bill finder makes on the routine sweep pages (scripts/bill-finder-ground-truth-2026-11.mjs). Until the v6 keys, no sweep page was about a mapped key, so any sweep mapping was false. The v6 keys (energy production, school choice, health care access, cutting spending) are ordinary campaign topics, so a sweep page can now name a real bill on its key. Each mapping here was read against the page and marked correct (the named bill is about the key, in a passage about it) or false. The report counts a sweep mapping that is not in this list, or is marked false, as a false mapping. Reviewed 2026-11-12. The v7 keys (climate and clean energy, gun safety, abortion, voting rules, housing, trade, wages and unions, criminal justice) are also ordinary campaign topics; their sweep mappings were read the same way on 2026-11-12. Three were false on first run and were fixed in the patterns, not marked here: a Vermont farm fund (S.60) read through "climate disasters", a union-election law read as a voting bill through "second election", and the 21st Century Cures Act read as criminal justice through "improve … our criminal justice system"; a Vermont state bill (S.100) read as a federal number is no longer mapped by the v7 keys on a state legislator's page. The v8 keys (Social Security, veterans, farming, privacy, drug prices, law enforcement, college costs, public lands) were read the same way on 2026-11-12. Three were false on first run and were fixed in the patterns, not marked here: the Affordable Care Act on a Talarico page moved from healthcare to drug prices (healthcare now keeps a sentence that names coverage), the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act read as a veterans bill through "Veterans’ Courts", and the New York Health Act read as a farm bill through the next sentence on a list page (an uncatalogued v8 measure now needs the key's subject in a sentence that names it or carries it on).

reviewed.why: A campaign issue page; the passage on health coverage (a public option, caps on costs) names the Affordable Care Act, a health coverage law.
"Protect and improve the Affordable Care Act (ACA) and reverse … cuts to the ACA": the ACA, on health coverage.

reviewed.bill: Cornyn-Supported Working Families Tax Cuts Act
reviewed.why: His health care issue page lists a release headlined "Funding Made Possible Through Cornyn-Supported Working Families Tax Cuts Act" (the finder keeps the "Cornyn-Supported" lead-in of the headline in the name): health funding from the Working Families Tax Cut Act (the 2025 reconciliation law, which changed Medicaid and created a rural health fund).
The same page lists his op-ed "The Working Families Tax Cut Act Prescribes Real Remedies for Health Care": the same law, on health care.
"the Medicaid expansion under the Affordable Care Act": the ACA, on health coverage.
"Efforts to expand access have stalled in Washington (Medicare for All Act)": a health coverage bill, on access.

(v7) His health care page lists his cosponsorship of the Safeguarding Women from Chemical Abortion Act, "which would ban the chemical abortion drug mifepristone": an abortion bill. The finder starts the name after the possessive "Hawley (R-MO)’s" and keeps only "Chemical Abortion Act"; the bill is the right one.
(v7) "Make it easier to form a union by removing the second election from the Colorado Labor Peace Act": a state union-election law, on the right to organize.
(v7) The same law, named with a possessive, in the passage on organized labor and the minimum wage: "so that workers can form a union and a collective bargaining unit with one election".
(v7) "increase the supply of housing … legislation like the Minnesota Starter Home Act … helping increase the number of available duplexes and townhomes": a state housing-supply law.
(v7) "provide justice-involved veterans a second chance … the Veterans Restorative Justice Act": a state sentencing-alternative law for veterans.
(v7) "the gutting of the Voting Rights Act … which helps ensure everyone gets to vote": the voting-rights law, in a passage on voting access.

(v7) The passage on "common-sense gun laws" names the Protect Illinois Communities Act (the state's 2023 assault-weapons law). The finder reads "Protect" as a verb and keeps "Illinois Communities Act"; the bill is the right one.
(v7) "enforcing Illinois’ Reproductive Health Act" in the reproductive-rights passage: the state law protecting abortion access.
(v7) "Georgia Homegrown Solar Act … would have expanded Georgians’ access to community solar": a state clean-energy bill.

(v8) His health care page lists a release headlined "Legislation Would Crack Down on Patent System Abuse" on the Affordable Prescriptions for Patients Act, a bill against drug-patent abuse to bring generic drugs to market: a drug-price bill.
(v8) "the bipartisan Affordable Prescriptions for Patients Act , which would lower prescription drug costs": a drug-price bill.
